title: P300 dataset BI2015a from a "Brain Invaders" experiment
description: EEG recordings from 43 healthy participants playing Brain Invaders, a visual P300 brain-computer interface game based on an oddball paradigm with a grid of 36 symbols. Data were acquired with 32 wet electrodes across three sessions with flash durations of 50, 80 and 110 ms, to study the influence of flash duration on a calibration-less P300 BCI using an adaptive Riemannian classifier. Resting-state and eyes-closed recordings were also collected before and after the game sessions at GIPSA-lab, Grenoble.
methods_description: Participants played three game sessions of nine levels each with different flash durations (110, 80, 50 ms). EEG was recorded at 512 Hz from 32 wet Ag/AgCl electrodes (g.USBamp, g.tec; 10-10 montage; reference right earlobe, ground Fz) using OpenViBE with USB-synchronized tagging. A real-time adaptive Riemannian Minimum Distance to Mean classifier assessed commands without calibration. About one minute of resting state and eyes-closed data were recorded before and after the sessions.
